draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kovalam! The red-and-white lighthouse on the rocks has watched these three curved beaches since 1972. In the 1970s this was a stop on the hippie trail.
draft.hungryLine: Kovalam's beach restaurants lay out the day's catch on ice. Point, pick and they'll grill it.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Climb the lighthouse for the view over all three beaches, then walk to Hawa Beach.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Pick a beach café at sunset and let the waves do the talking.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Vizhinjam, just south of here, was a busy port of the Ay kings well over a thousand years ago.

legends.title: The beach that shocked Kerala
legends.body: In the 1970s this was one of the first beaches in India where foreign visitors sunbathed topless. The name stuck, though the practice didn't.

legends.title: A royal summer house
legends.body: The old palace on the hill was built in the 1920s for a Travancore royal. It later became part of a hotel.

tips.title: Respect the red flags.
tips.body: Monsoon seas here are rough from June to August.

tips.title: Fish is priced by weight.
tips.body: Ask for the price before it goes on the grill.

story.title: The Ay port
story.body: Vizhinjam, next door, was a port of the Ay kingdom. Traders sailed in from across the Arabian Sea.

story.title: A royal retreat
story.body: The Travancore royal family came to these quiet coves to escape the heat of the capital.

story.title: The hippie trail
story.body: Travellers heading across Asia found Kovalam, and its beaches became famous around the world.

story.title: The lighthouse
story.body: The Vizhinjam lighthouse was built on the rocks, and its stripes became Kovalam's postcard picture.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Lighthouse first, a swim, then grilled fish at sunset. Tell me what you picked off the ice.
